Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & concurrency — post-call recap / next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — great alignment on the app flow. Quick recap and our asks so we can size recommended configs and an initial quota proposal:

- Target SLOs you mentioned: p50 < 200ms (interactive chat), p95 < 750ms (end-to-end streaming).
- Peak traffic: you estimated ~500 req/s average peak with spikes up to ~1,000 concurrent active sessions.
- Typical payload: prompt ~200 input tokens, expected response ~300 tokens (streaming required).
- Connection model: browser clients via backend proxy (connection pooling possible); you asked about per-connection limits and keep-alive.

Next steps from Redwood: please share your traffic profile (minute-level sample for a typical day and peak day) and any firewall/proxy constraints. We'll turn that into two options: (1) hosted API with negotiated per-route quotas & burst settings, (2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) sizing + pricing.

I've attached a short doc with the concurrency options we typically propose for customers with streaming workloads. Proposed timing: engineering sync next week (30–45m) to walk traffic profile and connection pooling approach.

Attachments: redwood-concurrency-options.pdf

—

Thanks Marissa — that matches what we discussed. A few more concrete numbers from our side (attached sample traffic sheet):

- Typical peak: 500 req/s sustained for ~10m windows (business-critical), short bursts up to 1,200 req/s for ~30–60s.
- Concurrency: roughly 800–1,000 parallel open conversations during peaks; behind a set of 6 proxy nodes.
- Payload sizes: median input 180 tokens, median response 320 tokens; worst-case response up to 1,500 tokens (rare).
- Streaming: yes, SSE-based streaming from our backend to browsers. We expect end-to-end p95 < 750ms for interactive flows.
- Security: must pass our security questionnaire (we'll send it separately) and require audit logs for token usage.

Attached: acme-infra-profile.xlsx

Can you confirm Redwood's default hosted rate limit behavior (per-API-key, per-route, per-minute vs concurrency) and what you can do for burst allowances?

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & concurrency — post-call recap / next steps

Great — thanks for the spreadsheet, Anna. Initial responses and what we'll prepare for the engineering sync:

1) Hosted defaults: Redwood's hosted tier enforces per-key rate limits (token-based and request-based) plus soft concurrency limits to protect shared capacity. Defaults vary by account tier but typical values are: 200 concurrent requests and token-rate limits roughly aligned to 120k tokens/min for mid-tier accounts. These can be adjusted for PLG customers by request; for sustained higher concurrency we recommend Dedicated.

2) Burst handling: we support short burst windows via token-bucket bursting and can configure higher burst quotas per-route for authenticated clients.

3) Dedicated sizing: based on your numbers (500 sustained, 1,200 bursts, up to 1,000 concurrent), we'll size a Dedicated pool with headroom for 1.5–2x concurrency for safety. We'll provide two options: minimal commit (monthly) and reserved commit (3–12 months) for lower unit costs.

4) Streaming behavior: our streaming path preserves per-token latency; KV cache and batching are disabled for streaming routes unless explicitly configured. We'll need to discuss how your proxy aggregates/resends streaming chunks to end-users to ensure latency SLOs.

Attached is a short options doc (redwood-concurrency-options.pdf). For the sync, can you confirm availability: Tue/Wed next week 10–12 PT? I'll loop in Vivek and Rishi for the technical run-through. Also cc'ing our sales lead to follow procurement and SLA discussions.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & concurrency — technical notes on connection pooling & limits

Quick technical notes to set expectations before the call:

- Connection pooling: for browser->backend->Redwood setups we recommend long-lived keep-alive connections using HTTP/2 or gRPC where possible. Each connection can multiplex multiple concurrent requests; we recommend limiting per-connection outstanding requests to ~8–12 to avoid head-of-line scheduling at proxies.

- Multiple connections per proxy: given your 6 proxy nodes, plan to open 8–16 upstream connections per proxy to allow the load to spread and to avoid TCP connection churn.

- Per-connection limits vs gateway quotas: Redwood enforces per-key concurrency caps (requests in flight) and token throughput. Best practice: implement client-side pooling + small request queues (100–200ms allowance) to smooth bursts.

- Hosted vs Dedicated: Hosted can be tuned (we can raise soft quotas and set per-route burst allowances) but sustained 1,000 concurrent will likely require Dedicated with reserved capacity. As a rule of thumb: Hosted tier comfortable sustained concurrency ~200–300; Dedicated can be provisioned to 2k+ concurrent depending on commit level.

- Fallbacks: if rate limits are hit we return 429 with retry-after; for mission-critical paths we provide automatic fallback policies (e.g., route to a cheaper quantized model or queue requests) as part of Dedicated contracts.

I'll bring detailed numbers and an example capacity plan to the sync. Meanwhile, Marissa — can you capture ACME's proxy concurrency (open connections) and SSL termination details so we can finalize recommended per-connection settings?

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
